verses.zh: （称谢诗。）普天下当向耶和华欢呼！
verses.en: A thanksgiving psalm.Shout out praises to the Lord, all the earth!
verses.commentary:
100:1 The Psalms regularly express a universal aspect of Israel's God. He is the one
true God, creator, sustainer, redeemer (cf. Psalm 33; 47; 98).

The USB Handbook (p. 852) suggests that the phrase "all the earth" should be
understood with each of the poetic lines in Ps. 100:2-3.

verses.zh: 你们当乐意事奉耶和华，当来向他歌唱！
verses.en: Worship[NOTE:1] the Lord with joy.Enter his presence with joyful singing.
notes: Psalm 100. The psalmist celebrates the fact that Israel has a special relationship to God and summons worshipers to praise the Lord for his faithfulness.
verses.commentary:
100:2 In light of YHWH as the one and only God (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM) they

- serve Him with gladness, cf. Deut. 12:11-12; 28:47

- come before Him with joyful singing, cf. Ps. 66:1; 81:1; 95:2

Both of these IMPERATIVES (also Ps. 100:4) refer to temple worship.

▣ "with joyful singing" This FEMININE NOUN (BDB 943) refers to

- a shout of joy (i.e. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 1128)

- "cry of joy," cf. Job 3:7; 20:5; Ps. 63:5

verses.zh: 你们当晓得耶和华是　神！我们是他造的，也是属他的；我们是他的民，也是他草场的羊。
verses.en: Acknowledge that the Lord is God.He made us and we belong to him,[NOTE:1] we are his people, the sheep of his pasture.
verses.commentary:
100:3 "Know" This Hebrew root has a wide semantic field. Here, it denotes

- information about

- relationship with

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "the Lord Himself is God" This is
a recurrent theme of the uniqueness of YHWH (cf. Exod. 8:10; 9:14; Deut. 4:35,39; 1 Kgs. 18:39;
Ps. 46:10). There is only one God (cf. Deut. 6:4), but other spiritual beings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN

▣ "It is He who has made us" This refers
to the call and promise (including the exodus, cf. Gen. 15:12-21) to Abraham and
his descendants (see Contextual Insights, B).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣

NASB, NKJV, NJB, LXX, Peshitta
"and not we ourselves"

NRSV, TEV, JPSOA, REB, Vulgate
"and we are His"

The first option (NASB) follows the MT (Kethiv). The second (NRSV) is
a suggestion made by the Masoretic scholars who compiled the MT (Qere).
The UBS Text Project (p. 373) gives the Qere a "B" rating (some doubt).

The problem is whether "and not" is a PREPOSITION, "His"
or a CONJUNCTION and a negative. Both would sound exactly alike when read.

▣ "His people and the sheep of His pasture" This is imagery for YHWH's special covenant people
(cf. Ps. 74:1; 79:13; 80:1; 95:7; 100:3).

verses.zh: 当称谢进入他的门；当赞美进入他的院。当感谢他，称颂他的名！
verses.en: Enter his gates with thanksgivingand his courts with praise.Give him thanks.Praise his name.

verses.zh: 因为耶和华本为善。他的慈爱存到永远；他的信实直到万代。
verses.en: For the Lord is good.His loyal love endures,[NOTE:1] and he is faithful through all generations.[NOTE:2]
notes: The present translation (like most modern translations) follows the Qere (marginal reading), which reads literally, “and to him [are] we.” The Kethib (consonantal text) has “and not we.” The suffixed preposition לוֹ (lo, “to him”) was confused aurally with the negative particle לֹא (loʾ, “not”) because the two sound identical.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This brief Psalm has seven IMPERATIVES directed at YHWH's people.

- shout, Ps. 100:1 ‒ BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil cf. Ps. 47:1; 95:1,2

- serve, Ps. 100:2 ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, Qal, cf. Exod. 3:12; 4:23; Deut. 6:13; 1 Sam. 7:3; 1 Chr. 28:9

- come, Ps. 100:2 ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal

- know (i.e., in the sense of "affirm in worship"), Ps. 100:3 ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal

- enter, Ps. 100:4 ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal, cf. Ps. 96:8

- give thanks, Ps. 100:4 ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil

- bless, Ps. 100:4 ‒ BDB 138, KB 159, Piel

- The only VERB (PERFECT) that is not an IMPERATIVE
is in Ps. 100:3b, which describes YHWH's election and deliverance of Israel (i.e., Gen. 12:1-3; 15:12-21).

- He made us ‒ Ps. 95:6; 119:73

- Israel is His flock - Ps. 23:1; 74:1; 95:7; Isa. 40:11; Jer. 31:10; Ezek. 34:31 (also a
Messianic reference, Ezek. 34:23; Micah 5:4; Zechariah 11; John 10:11,14-16)

- There is no VERBAL in Ps. 100:5. A "to be" VERB must be supplied.
Psalm 100:3b,c and 5 describe YHWH Himself and His redemptive activity.

- Some scholars (i.e., UBS Handbook, NASB Study Bible) believe this Psalm is the concluding
doxology of the "kingship Psalms" (i.e., Psalm 93; 95-99). The term "king" is not used, but Ps. 100:3b-c
may be an allusion to it.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

1Shout joyfully to the Lord, all the earth.

2Serve the Lord with gladness;

Come before Him with joyful singing.

3Know that the Lord Himself is God;
